Project, publication and use notice

Clinical Intelligence — The AI-Augmented Clinician is a personal book-thesis project developed as independent research. It is an experimental and educational work in progress, shared as an open publication through the project’s public GitHub repository. It does not represent an institutional position, endorsement, or completed clinical validation.

Project and author links: EMR Enhancer · CCIS · Contextual Interaction Platform (CIP) · Personal website · LinkedIn

DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24399214.

Suggested citation: Gupta, A. K. (2026). Clinical Intelligence — The AI-Augmented Clinician: A project-based book-thesis (Version 1.5; working manuscript). Independent researcher. https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24399214.

IMPORTANT DISCLAIMER — EXPERIMENTAL WORK FOR LEARNING PURPOSES ONLY

This book, its software examples, workflows, analytics, AI-assisted features, clinical content, pathways, rules, prototypes and demonstrations are experimental and are provided solely for learning, discussion and independent research. They are not medical advice, a clinical guideline, a validated medical device, or a substitute for professional judgement, institutional policy, supervision or applicable law. They must not be used to diagnose, treat, monitor, triage or make decisions about real patients, and must not be relied upon in live clinical care.

Any clinical examples are illustrative unless explicitly identified and supported by authoritative sources. Implementations may be incomplete, inaccurate, insecure or unsuitable for deployment. AI-generated material may be wrong, fabricated, biased or out of date. Verify all facts, code, references, calculations, terminology, safety controls and regulatory obligations independently. Do not enter identifiable patient information or confidential health data into public demos, repositories or third-party AI services. Any future clinical use would require appropriate clinical governance, privacy and security review, hazard analysis, validation, monitoring, and regulatory assessment in the relevant jurisdiction.

The author shares this work as an independent researcher and accepts no implication that the material is institutionally approved or clinically validated. Users are responsible for their own assessment and use. Where the repository or manuscript describes implemented behaviour, that description should be checked against the current source code and deployment configuration; planned designs and recommendations are not claims of implemented functionality.
